nota: Curated selection of the most important AI sites worldwide for the fixed layer 'AI infrastructure' (fixed-installation schema). Every entry is a copy of a point in ai-mondo.json (field rif_ai_mondo), chosen in raccolta/ai/ai_selezione.json; ids of the November 2026 US dossier are kept. Categories mapped to the map's AI_CAT: data-center, fab-chip (fabs, packaging, equipment), supercomputer.

punti.origine_coord: estimated: OSM Nominatim geocoding of 'Houli, Taichung, Taiwan'
punti.note: DRAM (1-gamma) and HBM. Owner: Micron Technology. Micron's largest Taiwan base (DRAM front-end and HBM back-end). A second advanced packaging facility starts HBM production in mid-October 2026. Micron says it has invested over NT$1.6 trillion (about 50 bn USD) in Taiwan. Most 2027 HBM output is already under contract.

punti.origine_coord: estimated: OSM geocoding of Zhangjiang (SMIC headquarters); the 7/5 nm lines have no public location
punti.note: 7 nm (N+2), 5 nm in trial; no EUV. Owner: SMIC. Partly operational. SemiAnalysis estimate: 7 nm-and-below capacity under 45,000 wafers per month at end-2025, 60,000 in 2026. Makes the Huawei Ascend chips; the stated constraint is HBM memory, not the foundry. China reportedly aims to quintuple 7/5 nm output (TrendForce). Analyst numbers, not official.

punti.origine_coord: estimated: OSM Nominatim geocoding of 'Hefei, Anhui, China'
punti.note: DRAM (DDR5, LPDDR5), early HBM. Owner: ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT). China's main DRAM maker. Reports put CXMT at about 320,000 wafers/month, rising to 420,000 by 2027 (Nikkei via Tom's Hardware); HBM capacity only about 5,000 wafers/month (SemiAnalysis). Hefei and Beijing plants reported at full capacity.

Fab 2: in February 2026 TSMC announced the switch to 3 nm (Taiwan approved on 2026-03-31), target 2028; signs of a slower construction site. Amount = public R&D support approved (2,354 bn JPY, April 2026); another source cites about 2,900 bn JPY planned. Single site, no backup.

punti.note: 28/22 nm and 16/12 nm FinFET. Owner: ESMC (TSMC 70%). Topping-out in September 2026. Tool move-in shifted to H2 2027 (dpa-AFX correction of 2026-09-14): realistic production in 2028. 40,000 wafers per month. German state aid approved by the EU. Chips for cars and industry, not for GPUs.
